fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH CUTS (rockfish species, FT-NIR ages already in a stock assessment, paper details, the word annuli). Atomic claims, one fact each, every one re-read on the cited NOAA page by the validator.

claims.claim: The archive holds 2.5 million otolith pairs.
claims.verbatim_source: "an enormous archive of 2.5 million otolith pairs dating back to the 1960s."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: say per NOAA on screen
never say every sample is from Alaska waters (surveys run California to Alaska)

claims.claim: The archive dates back to the 1960s.
claims.verbatim_source: "an enormous archive of 2.5 million otolith pairs dating back to the 1960s."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: never stack with 'four decades'

claims.claim: Center researchers age more than 30,000 otoliths a year under microscopes.
claims.verbatim_source: "Back in Seattle, Alaska Fisheries Science Center researchers analyze more than 30,000 under microscopes to count annual growth rings."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: never mix with the 2023 'up to 40,000' figure

claims.claim: Age is read by counting annual growth rings, like tree rings.
claims.verbatim_source: "Counting otolith growth zones to estimate fish age is analogous to counting tree rings."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: say annual growth rings, never annuli

claims.claim: The oldest-aged rockfish's otolith was collected in 2022 during an Aleutian Islands survey.
claims.verbatim_source: "Collected in 2022 during a survey in the Aleutian Islands, this fish was born in 1878."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: say a rockfish, never a species

claims.claim: That rockfish is estimated at 144 years old, born in 1878, the oldest aged at the Center.
claims.verbatim_source: "An otolith collected from a rockfish (the oldest to be aged at the Center), estimated to be 144 years old."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: say estimated
oldest aged at the Center, never oldest fish
never imply this fish was machine-aged

claims.claim: Near-infrared light makes a spectral signature that machine learning correlates to age.
claims.verbatim_source: "Near-infrared light generates spectral signatures from otoliths that machine-learning algorithms correlate directly to age."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES

claims.verbatim_source: "Fourier Transform Near-Infrared Spectroscopy increases efficiency 600 - 800 percent for examining otoliths to determine fish age."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: say per NOAA
pair with c9 on screen or in VO nearby
never combine with the 2023 10x figure

claims.claim: Conventional ageing is still part of the process.
claims.verbatim_source: "While conventional ageing is still part of the process"
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: never say AI replaced human readers

claims.claim: In 2023 NOAA reported models trained and tested on 8,617 walleye pollock otoliths collected 2014 to 2018.
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES (2023)
requires: label 2023

claims.verbatim_source: "It takes just 30–50 seconds per otolith to estimate the age of the fish."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES (2023)
requires: label 2023
never with the 600 to 800 percent as one measurement

claims.claim: Around 2 million pairs once sat in a 1930s wooden airplane hangar in Seattle, now part of NOAA's Western Regional Center.
claims.verbatim_source: "Around 2 million pairs of otoliths once sat inside a 1930s wooden airplane hangar that's now part of NOAA's Western Regional Center in Seattle."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: around 2 million, never 2.5 for the hangar

claims.claim: In 2012 an NSF grant let NOAA and the Burke Museum relocate them to the UW Fish Collection.
claims.verbatim_source: "In 2012, a National Science Foundation grant allowed NOAA and the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture to relocate them."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES

claims.claim: In 2023 NOAA named use of these ages in stock assessment models as the next step.
claims.verbatim_source: "The next step is to use these new age data products in stock assessment models."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES (2023)
requires: never claim machine ages are already in an assessment

claims.claim: Age composition is used to set sustainable catch limits each year, by resource managers.
claims.verbatim_source: "Knowing the age composition of commercially exploited fish populations is critical to determine fish population size and set sustainable catch limits each year."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: managers set limits, never the AI

claims.claim: Derek Chamberlin, supervisory research fisheries biologist, AFSC Age and Growth Program: otoliths are a perfect little time capsule.
claims.verbatim_source: "Otoliths are a perfect little time capsule."
claims.label: DEREK CHAMBERLIN · NOAA FISHERIES
requires: attribute on screen to Chamberlin, plate only, no face

claims.claim: Otoliths are fish ear stones, collected in pairs.
claims.verbatim_source: "We are using AI and near-Infrared analysis of otoliths (ear stones) to age Alaska pollock"
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES

claims.claim: Scientists spent a decade analyzing tens of thousands of archive samples to train the AI models.
claims.verbatim_source: "Scientists spent a decade analyzing tens of thousands of physical samples from the archive to train these AI models."
claims.label: PER NOAA FISHERIES
requires: single-page source, keep the wording general

cut: FT-NIR ages already used in a stock assessment
